description: A collection manager needs to clean up incomplete accession records so object identity, provenance details, storage location, and accession numbering are consistent across the catalog. All institutions and objects are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 37-year-old museum registrar inheriting a backlog of partially standardized records
user_profile.context: The collection is usable day to day, but record inconsistency is creating growing long-term risk
user_profile.communication_style: Meticulous and records-oriented, wants normalization rules applied consistently

fact_sheet.fact: Dr. Aris Thorne is the Registrar at the Veridian Gallery of Natural History, hired on May 15, 2023.
The Head Collections Manager, who supervises Dr. Thorne, is Elara Vance.
The Veridian Gallery uses a custom-built collection management system (CMS) named 'Catalogix Pro'.
The login URL for the production instance of Catalogix Pro is https://veridian.catalogix.local/login.
Prior to 2018, accession numbers were formatted inconsistently, with examples including '98.12.a', '1998-12-b', and 'A98.12'.
The new standard for accession numbers, effective January 1, 2018, is YYYY.##.## (e.g., 2024.01.01 for the first object lot of the year).
Object record '03.157', a Pterodactylus fossil cast, is missing its 'Date Acquired' and 'Acquisition Method' fields.
The object '1999-42-c', a collection of Cambrian trilobite fossils, has its dimensions recorded in inches (12" x 8") instead of the standard centimeters.
The provenance for object 2005.18.01 (a polished ammonite) lists the donor simply as 'J. Smith', with no contact information or deed of gift on file.
Accession 'A95.04' (a set of Miocene shark teeth) has a conflicting 'Previous Collection' field, listing both 'Blackwood Institute' and 'Dr. Alistair Finch Collection'.
The Paleontology Compact Storage is located in room B-112 in the museum's basement.
Storage location data in Catalogix Pro uses mixed formats, including 'Shelf 3A, Cab 12', 'B112-C12-S3A', and 'Basement, Cabinet 12, Shelf 3-A'.
The standardized storage location format is BUILDING-ROOM-ROW-CABINET-SHELF (e.g., MAIN-B112-R04-C12-S03).
The data cleanup initiative is officially titled 'Project Nightingale'.
The primary goal of Project Nightingale is to standardize all 12,542 accession records created before January 1, 2018.
The deadline for completing Project Nightingale is December 31, 2025.
Project Nightingale tasks and progress are tracked using a Jira board at https://jira.veridian.local/projects/NIGHT.
For technical issues with Catalogix Pro, the designated IT support contact is Lena Petrova at l.petrova@veridiangallery.org, extension 4401.
A collections intern, Samuel Chen, has been assigned to Project Nightingale for 20 hours per week, starting September 1, 2024.
The record for '2011.07.b' (a fossilized fern leaf) has three low-resolution (72 dpi) JPG images; the standard requires 300 dpi TIFF files.
The 'Condition Report Date' field is now mandatory for all new accessions and must be populated for all 12,542 records in Project Nightingale.
The current version of Catalogix Pro being used is v3.4.1, which lacks a bulk-editing feature for provenance fields.
Accession 2001.22.05 (a Cretaceous amber specimen) is marked as a 'Gift' but the scanned Deed of Gift document (PDF) is not linked in the record.
Cabinet 14 in room B-112 contains 32 objects whose physical location labels do not match their digital records in Catalogix Pro.
Dr. Aris Thorne's workstation for this project is R-204 in the Collections Management office suite.
A key milestone for Project Nightingale is to complete the standardization of all 845 records from the 'Blackwood Institute' donation by October 31, 2024.
Object descriptions for accessions prior to 2010 often use subjective terms like 'good condition' instead of the required Getty AAT terminology.
For questions regarding the 'Dr. Alistair Finch Collection', the point of contact is his estate's executor, Miriam Finch, at m.finch.estate@emailprovider.net.
The Catalogix Pro database server, 'VGNH-DB01', is backed up nightly at 2:00 AM, with backups retained for 30 days.
The insurance valuation for object '99.01.a' (a complete mosasaur skull) is listed as '$50,000' and was last updated on June 5, 2002.
A progress report for Project Nightingale is due to Elara Vance by 5:00 PM on the last Friday of every month.
